sanskrit: naitādṛśo dṛṣṭapūrvaḥ saṃgrāmo naiva ca śrutaḥ droṇasyābhāvabhāveṣu prasaktānāṃ yathābhavat
english: Never before had such a battle been seen, nor even heard of, as the one that broke out among those who were caught up in the doubt of whether Droṇa lived or was no more.

sanskrit: idaṃ ghoram idaṃ citram idaṃ raudram iti prabho tatra yuddhāny adṛśyanta pratatāni bahūni ca
english: "This is terrible, this is wondrous, this is fierce!"—so men cried, O lord, and there many a combat was seen, drawn out and beyond counting.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca teṣv evaṃ saṃnivṛtteṣu pratyudyāteṣu bhāgaśaḥ kathaṃ yuyudhire pārthā māmakāś ca tarasvinaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When those warriors had thus turned back and advanced again in their several divisions, how did the swift sons of Pṛthā and my own men do battle?

sanskrit: kim arjunaś cāpy akarot saṃśaptakabalaṃ prati saṃśaptakā vā pārthasya kim akurvata saṃjaya
english: And what did Arjuna do against the host of the Saṃśaptakas, and what, Saṃjaya, did the Saṃśaptakas do against the son of Pṛthā?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tathā teṣu nivṛtteṣu pratyudyāteṣu bhāgaśaḥ svayam abhyadravad bhīmaṃ nāgānīkena te sutaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When they had thus turned back and advanced again in their several divisions, your son himself rushed upon Bhīma with a corps of elephants.

sanskrit: sa nāga iva nāgena govṛṣeṇeva govṛṣaḥ samāhūtaḥ svayaṃ rājñā nāgānīkam upādravat
english: And Bhīma, challenged by the king himself—as elephant meets elephant, as bull meets bull—charged that corps of elephants in turn.

sanskrit: sa yuddhakuśalaḥ pārtho bāhuvīryeṇa cānvitaḥ abhinat kuñjarānīkam acireṇaiva māriṣa
english: That son of Pṛthā, skilled in war and endowed with the strength of his arms, shattered the corps of elephants in but a moment, O venerable one.

sanskrit: te gajā girisaṃkāśāḥ kṣarantaḥ sarvato madam bhīmasenasya nārācair vimukhā vimadīkṛtāḥ
english: Those elephants, huge as hills, oozing rut on every side, were turned back by Bhīmasena's iron shafts and stripped of their frenzy.

sanskrit: vidhamed abhrajālāni yathā vāyuḥ samantataḥ vyadhamat tāny anīkāni tathaiva pavanātmajaḥ
english: As the wind scatters the masses of cloud on every side, so did the son of the Wind scatter those formations.

sanskrit: sa teṣu visṛjan bāṇān bhīmo nāgeṣv aśobhata bhuvaneṣv iva sarveṣu gabhastīn udito raviḥ
english: Loosing his arrows among those elephants, Bhīma shone like the risen sun casting its rays over all the worlds.

sanskrit: te bhīmabāṇaiḥ śataśaḥ saṃsyūtā vibabhur gajāḥ gabhastibhir ivārkasya vyomni nānābalāhakāḥ
english: Pierced by Bhīma's arrows in their hundreds, those elephants shone like the varied clouds in the sky shot through by the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: tathā gajānāṃ kadanaṃ kurvāṇam anilātmajam kruddho duryodhano 'bhyetya pratyavidhyac chitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: As the son of the Wind wrought such havoc among the elephants, Duryodhana in fury drew near and struck him back with sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṣaṇena kṣitipaṃ kṣatajapratimekṣaṇaḥ kṣayaṃ ninīṣur niśitair bhīmo vivyādha patribhiḥ
english: Then in an instant Bhīma, his eyes red as blood and bent on the king's destruction, pierced that lord of earth with keen feathered shafts.

sanskrit: sa śarārpitasarvāṅgaḥ kruddho vivyādha pāṇḍavam nārācair arkaraśmyābhair bhīmasenaṃ smayann iva
english: His every limb studded with arrows, Duryodhana in wrath pierced the Pāṇḍava in return, smiting Bhīmasena with iron shafts bright as the sun's rays, and smiling the while.

sanskrit: tasya nāgaṃ maṇimayaṃ ratnacitraṃ dhvaje sthitam bhallābhyāṃ kārmukaṃ caiva kṣipraṃ ciccheda pāṇḍavaḥ
english: With two broad-headed shafts the Pāṇḍava swiftly cut away the jewelled elephant, gleaming with gems, that stood upon his banner, and his bow as well.

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ pīḍyamānaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmena māriṣa cukṣobhayiṣur abhyāgād aṅgo mātaṅgam āsthitaḥ
english: Seeing Duryodhana hard pressed by Bhīma, O venerable one, the king of the Aṅgas, mounted upon an elephant, came on, eager to throw Bhīma into confusion.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ mātaṅgam ambudapratimasvanam kumbhāntare bhīmaseno nārācenārdayad bhṛśam
english: As that elephant, with a trumpeting like the roar of a raincloud, came rushing on, Bhīmasena struck it hard between its frontal lobes with an iron shaft.

sanskrit: tasya kāyaṃ vinirbhidya mamajja dharaṇītale tataḥ papāta dvirado vajrāhata ivācalaḥ
english: Piercing through its body, the shaft sank into the earth, and the elephant fell like a mountain struck by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tasyāvarjitanāgasya mlecchasyāvapatiṣyataḥ śiraś ciccheda bhallena kṣiprakārī vṛkodaraḥ
english: And as that barbarian, his elephant toppling, was himself about to fall, swift-handed Vṛkodara severed his head with a broad-headed shaft.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite vīre saṃprādravata sā camūḥ saṃbhrāntāśvadviparathā padātīn avamṛdnatī
english: When that hero had fallen, that host broke and fled, its horses, elephants, and chariots in panic, trampling down its own foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: teṣv anīkeṣu sarveṣu vidravatsu samantataḥ prāgjyotiṣas tato bhīmaṃ kuñjareṇa samādravat
english: And while all those formations were fleeing on every side, the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa then charged Bhīma upon his elephant.

sanskrit: yena nāgena maghavān ajayad daityadānavān sa nāgapravaro bhīmaṃ sahasā samupādravat
english: That foremost of elephants—the very one on which Maghavan had conquered the Daityas and Dānavas—now rushed of a sudden upon Bhīma.

sanskrit: śravaṇābhyām atho padbhyāṃ saṃhatena kareṇa ca vyāvṛttanayanaḥ kruddhaḥ pradahann iva pāṇḍavam
english: With its ears, its feet, and its coiled trunk, eyes rolling and enraged, it seemed as if it would burn the Pāṇḍava to ash.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvasya sainyasya nādaḥ samabhavan mahān hā hā vinihato bhīmaḥ kuñjareṇeti māriṣa
english: Then there arose a mighty cry from the whole army: "Alas, alas! Bhīma is slain by the elephant!"—so it ran, O venerable one.

sanskrit: tena nādena vitrastā pāṇḍavānām anīkinī sahasābhyadravad rājan yatra tasthau vṛkodaraḥ
english: Alarmed by that cry, O king, the host of the Pāṇḍavas rushed of a sudden to where Vṛkodara stood.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā hataṃ matvā vṛkodaram bhagadattaṃ sapāñcālaḥ sarvataḥ samavārayat
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, believing Vṛkodara slain, together with the Pāñcālas hemmed in Bhagadatta on every side.

sanskrit: taṃ rathai rathināṃ śreṣṭhāḥ parivārya samantataḥ avākirañ śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Surrounding him on all sides with their chariots, those foremost of chariot-warriors showered him with sharp arrows by the hundred and by the thousand.

sanskrit: sa vighātaṃ pṛṣatkānām aṅkuśena samācaran gajena pāṇḍupāñcālān vyadhamat parvateśvaraḥ
english: Warding off those shafts with his goad, the lord of the mountain land scattered the Pāṇḍus and Pāñcālas with his elephant.

sanskrit: tad adbhutam apaśyāma bhagadattasya saṃyuge tathā vṛddhasya caritaṃ kuñjareṇa viśāṃ pate
english: A marvel we beheld in that battle, O lord of peoples—such was the feat of the aged Bhagadatta with his elephant.

sanskrit: tato rājā daśārṇānāṃ prāgjyotiṣam upādravat tiryagyātena nāgena samadenāśugāminā
english: Then the king of the Daśārṇas charged the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa with his elephant—a rutting beast, swift-moving, advancing aslant.

sanskrit: tayor yuddhaṃ samabhavan nāgayor bhīmarūpayoḥ sapakṣayoḥ parvatayor yathā sadrumayoḥ purā
english: A battle arose between those two elephants of terrible form, as of old between two winged mountains clad with trees.

sanskrit: prāgjyotiṣapater nāgaḥ saṃnipatyāpavṛtya ca pārśve daśārṇādhipater bhittvā nāgam apātayat
english: The elephant of the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa, closing in and then wheeling about, pierced the elephant of the lord of the Daśārṇas in the flank and brought it down.

sanskrit: tomaraiḥ sūryaraśmyābhair bhagadatto 'tha saptabhiḥ jaghāna dviradasthaṃ taṃ śatruṃ pracalitāsanam
english: Then with seven lances bright as the sun's rays, Bhagadatta struck down that foe upon his elephant, shaken now from his seat.

sanskrit: upasṛtya tu rājānaṃ bhagadattaṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ rathānīkena mahatā sarvataḥ paryavārayat
english: But Yudhiṣṭhira, drawing near to King Bhagadatta, encircled him on every side with a great corps of chariots.

sanskrit: sa kuñjarastho rathibhiḥ śuśubhe sarvato vṛtaḥ parvate vanamadhyastho jvalann iva hutāśanaḥ
english: Mounted on his elephant and ringed about on all sides by chariot-warriors, he shone like a blazing fire set amid the forest upon a mountain.

sanskrit: maṇḍalaṃ sarvataḥ śliṣṭaṃ rathinām ugradhanvinām kiratāṃ śaravarṣāṇi sa nāgaḥ paryavartata
english: That elephant wheeled within the close-knit ring of fierce-bowed chariot-warriors as they poured down their showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāgjyotiṣo rājā parigṛhya dviparṣabham preṣayām āsa sahasā yuyudhānarathaṃ prati
english: Then the king of Prāgjyotiṣa, gathering up that bull among elephants, sent it of a sudden against the chariot of Yuyudhāna.

sanskrit: śineḥ pautrasya tu rathaṃ parigṛhya mahādvipaḥ abhicikṣepa vegena yuyudhānas tv apākramat
english: Seizing the chariot of the grandson of Śini, the great elephant hurled it away with force; but Yuyudhāna leaped clear.

sanskrit: bṛhataḥ saindhavān aśvān samutthāpya tu sārathiḥ tasthau sātyakim āsādya saṃplutas taṃ rathaṃ punaḥ
english: His charioteer, raising up the great Saindhava horses, reached Sātyaki, and leaping aboard once more, stood firm with him in the chariot again.

sanskrit: sa tu labdhvāntaraṃ nāgas tvarito rathamaṇḍalāt niścakrāma tataḥ sarvān paricikṣepa pārthivān
english: That elephant, having found its opening, swiftly broke forth from the ring of chariots and then flung down all the kings about it.

sanskrit: te tv āśugatinā tena trāsyamānā nararṣabhāḥ tam ekaṃ dviradaṃ saṃkhye menire śataśo nṛpāḥ
english: Terrified by that swift-moving beast, those bulls among men, those hundreds of kings, deemed that one elephant in the battle to be a hundred.

sanskrit: te gajasthena kālyante bhagadattena pāṇḍavāḥ airāvatasthena yathā devarājena dānavāḥ
english: The Pāṇḍavas were driven before Bhagadatta upon his elephant, as the Dānavas before the king of the gods mounted on Airāvata.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ pradravatāṃ bhīmaḥ pāñcālānām itas tataḥ gajavājikṛtaḥ śabdaḥ sumahān samajāyata
english: As the Pāñcālas fled hither and thither before him, a tremendous din arose, made by elephants and horses.

sanskrit: bhagadattena samare kālyamāneṣu pāṇḍuṣu prāgjyotiṣam abhikruddhaḥ punar bhīmaḥ samabhyayāt
english: As the Pāṇḍus were driven before Bhagadatta in the battle, Bhīma in fury charged the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa once again.

sanskrit: tasyābhidravato vāhān hastamuktena vāriṇā siktvā vyatrāsayan nāgas te pārtham aharaṃs tataḥ
english: As Bhīma charged, the elephant drenched his horses with water flung from its trunk and frighted them, and so they bore the son of Pṛthā away.

sanskrit: tatas tam abhyayāt tūrṇaṃ ruciparvākṛtīsutaḥ samukṣañ śaravarṣeṇa rathastho 'ntakasaṃnibhaḥ
english: Then the son of Ruciparvan, like unto Death and standing upon his chariot, charged the elephant swiftly, drenching it with a shower of arrows.

sanskrit: tato ruciraparvāṇaṃ śareṇa nataparvaṇā suparvā parvatapatir ninye vaivasvatakṣayam
english: Then with a smooth-jointed arrow the lord of the mountain Suparvan sent Ruciraparvan to the abode of the son of the Sun, Yama.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite vīre saubhadro draupadīsutāḥ cekitāno dhṛṣṭaketur yuyutsuś cārdayan dvipam
english: When that hero had fallen, the son of Subhadrā, the sons of Draupadī, Cekitāna, Dhṛṣṭaketu, and Yuyutsu fell upon the elephant and harried it.

sanskrit: ta enaṃ śaradhārābhir dhārābhir iva toyadāḥ siṣicur bhairavān nādān vinadanto jighāṃsavaḥ
english: They drenched it with streams of arrows, as raincloud's drench with downpours, roaring terrible cries and bent upon its slaughter.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārṣṇyaṅkuśāṅguṣṭhaiḥ kṛtinā codito dvipaḥ prasāritakaraḥ prāyāt stabdhakarṇekṣaṇo drutam
english: Then, urged on by the skilled driver with heel and goad and thumb, the elephant, trunk outstretched, ears and eyes rigid, charged swiftly forward.

sanskrit: so 'dhiṣṭhāya padā vāhān yuyutsoḥ sūtam ārujat putras tu tava saṃbhrāntaḥ saubhadrasyāpluto ratham
english: Treading down the horses of Yuyutsu with its feet, it crushed his charioteer; but your son, in confusion, sprang onto the chariot of Subhadrā's son.

sanskrit: sa kuñjarastho visṛjann iṣūn ariṣu pārthivaḥ babhau raśmīn ivādityo bhuvaneṣu samutsṛjan
english: That king, mounted on his elephant and loosing his shafts among his foes, shone like the sun casting his rays across the worlds.

sanskrit: tam ārjunir dvādaśabhir yuyutsur daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ tribhis tribhir draupadeyā dhṛṣṭaketuś ca vivyadhuḥ
english: Arjuna's son pierced him with twelve arrows, Yuyutsu with ten, and the sons of Draupadī and Dhṛṣṭaketu each with three.

sanskrit: so 'riyatnārpitair bāṇair ācito dvirado babhau saṃsyūta iva sūryasya raśmibhir jalado mahān
english: That elephant, studded with the arrows driven home by his foes' striving, shone like a great cloud shot through by the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: niyantuḥ śilpayatnābhyāṃ preṣito 'riśarārditaḥ paricikṣepa tān nāgaḥ sa ripūn savyadakṣiṇam
english: Driven by the skill and effort of its master, though tormented by the foes' arrows, that elephant flung down those enemies to left and right.

sanskrit: gopāla iva daṇḍena yathā paśugaṇān vane āveṣṭayata tāṃ senāṃ bhagadattas tathā muhuḥ
english: As a herdsman with his staff drives the herds of beasts together in the forest, so did Bhagadatta hem in that army again and again.

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ śyenābhipannānāṃ vāyasānām iva svanaḥ babhūva pāṇḍaveyānāṃ bhṛśaṃ vidravatāṃ svanaḥ
english: Swift as the clamor of crows fallen upon by a hawk was the clamor of the Pāṇḍavas as they fled in utter rout.

sanskrit: sa nāgarājaḥ pravarāṅkuśāhataḥ; purā sapakṣo 'drivaro yathā nṛpa bhayaṃ tathā ripuṣu samādadhad bhṛśaṃ; vaṇiggaṇānāṃ kṣubhito yathārṇavaḥ
english: That king of elephants, struck by the foremost of goads, was like a winged mountain of old, O king; and it sowed deep terror among the foes, as the storm-tossed ocean among bands of merchants.

sanskrit: tato dhvanir dviradarathāśvapārthivair; bhayād dravadbhir janito 'tibhairavaḥ kṣitiṃ viyad dyāṃ vidiśo diśas tathā; samāvṛṇot pārthiva saṃyuge tadā
english: Then a most fearful din, raised by elephants, chariots, horses, and kings fleeing in terror, filled the earth, the air, the heavens, and all the quarters and their bounds, O lord, in that battle.

sanskrit: sa tena nāgapravareṇa pārthivo; bhṛśaṃ jagāhe dviṣatām anīkinīm purā suguptāṃ vibudhair ivāhave; virocano devavarūthinīm iva
english: With that foremost of elephants, the king plunged deep into the host of his foes, as of old Virocana into the well-guarded army of the gods in battle, defended though it was by the wise ones.

sanskrit: bhṛśaṃ vavau jvalanasakho viyad rajaḥ; samāvṛṇon muhur api caiva sainikān tam ekanāgaṃ gaṇaśo yathā gajāḥ; samantato drutam iva menire janāḥ
english: The friend of fire, the wind, blew strongly, and the dust shrouded the sky and again and again the soldiers; and men deemed that one elephant to be a whole troop of elephants charging swiftly on every side.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yan māṃ pārthasya saṃgrāme karmāṇi paripṛcchasi tac chṛṇuṣva mahārāja pārtho yad akaron mṛdhe
english: Saṃjaya said: Since you ask me of the deeds of the son of Pṛthā in the battle, hear now, O great king, what Pārtha did in the fray.

sanskrit: rajo dṛṣṭvā samudbhūtaṃ śrutvā ca gajanisvanam bhajyatāṃ bhagadattena kaunteyaḥ kṛṣṇam abravīt
english: Seeing the dust risen up and hearing the trumpeting of the elephant as his men were broken by Bhagadatta, the son of Kuntī spoke to Kṛṣṇa:

sanskrit: yathā prāgjyotiṣo rājā gajena madhusūdana tvaramāṇo 'bhyatikrānto dhruvaṃ tasyaiṣa nisvanaḥ
english: "By the way the king of Prāgjyotiṣa has pressed swiftly forward with his elephant, O slayer of Madhu, this surely is the sound of that beast."

sanskrit: indrād anavaraḥ saṃkhye gajayānaviśāradaḥ prathamo vā dvitīyo vā pṛthivyām iti me matiḥ
english: "In battle he is not inferior to Indra, and skilled in elephant-craft; first upon the earth, or second—such is my judgment of him."

sanskrit: sa cāpi dviradaśreṣṭhaḥ sadāpratigajo yudhi sarvaśabdātigaḥ saṃkhye kṛtakarmā jitaklamaḥ
english: "And that finest of elephants, never matched by any rival elephant in war, unshaken by every sound in battle, proven in its deeds and tireless—"

sanskrit: sahaḥ śastranipātānām agnisparśasya cānagha sa pāṇḍavabalaṃ vyaktam adyaiko nāśayiṣyati
english: "—able to endure the fall of weapons and the touch of fire, O sinless one, that beast alone will plainly destroy the Pāṇḍava host this very day."

sanskrit: na cāvābhyām ṛte 'nyo 'sti śaktas taṃ pratibādhitum tvaramāṇas tato yāhi yataḥ prāgjyotiṣādhipaḥ
english: "And save we two there is no other able to withstand it; therefore make haste and drive to where the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa is."

sanskrit: śakrasakhyād dvipabalair vayasā cāpi vismitam adyainaṃ preṣayiṣyāmi balahantuḥ priyātithim
english: "Proud through his friendship with Śakra, through the strength of his elephants, and through his years—him will I send this day, a welcome guest, to the slayer of Bala."

sanskrit: vacanād atha kṛṣṇas tu prayayau savyasācinaḥ dāryate bhagadattena yatra pāṇḍavavāhinī
english: Then at the word of Savyasācin, Kṛṣṇa drove on to where the Pāṇḍava army was being rent apart by Bhagadatta.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntaṃ tataḥ paścād āhvayanto mahārathāḥ saṃśaptakāḥ samārohan sahasrāṇi caturdaśa
english: As he set forth, the Saṃśaptakas, those great chariot-warriors, fourteen thousand strong, came up behind, calling him to combat.

sanskrit: daśaiva tu sahasrāṇi trigartānāṃ narādhipa catvāri tu sahasrāṇi vāsudevasya ye 'nugāḥ
english: Ten thousand of them were Trigartas, O lord of men, and four thousand were those who followed Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: dāryamāṇāṃ camūṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagadattena māriṣa āhūyamānasya ca tair abhavad dhṛdayaṃ dvidhā
english: Seeing his army being rent apart by Bhagadatta, O venerable one, and being challenged by the Saṃśaptakas, Arjuna's heart was torn in two.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu śreyaskaraṃ karma bhaved iti vicintayan ito vā vinivarteyaṃ gaccheyaṃ vā yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Pondering which course would prove the more profitable—"Shall I turn back from here, or shall I go on to Yudhiṣṭhira?"—

sanskrit: tasya buddhyā vicāryaitad arjunasya kurūdvaha abhavad bhūyasī buddhiḥ saṃśaptakavadhe sthirā
english: weighing this in his mind, O foremost of the Kurus, Arjuna's stronger resolve settled firm upon the slaying of the Saṃśaptakas.

sanskrit: sa saṃnivṛttaḥ sahasā kapipravaraketanaḥ eko rathasahasrāṇi nihantuṃ vāsavī raṇe
english: He whose banner bore the foremost of apes turned suddenly back, the son of Vāsava, alone, to slay thousands of chariots in the fray.

sanskrit: sā hi duryodhanasyāsīn matiḥ karṇasya cobhayoḥ arjunasya vadhopāye tena dvaidham akalpayat
english: For such was the design of both Duryodhana and Karṇa, contrived as a means to Arjuna's slaying; by it they had wrought this division.

sanskrit: sa tu saṃvartayām āsa dvaidhībhāvena pāṇḍavaḥ rathena tu rathāgryāṇām akarot tāṃ mṛṣā tadā
english: But the Pāṇḍava turned that very division back upon them, and with his single chariot he made the design of those foremost of chariot-warriors come to nothing.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatasahasrāṇi śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām vyasṛjann arjune rājan saṃśaptakamahārathāḥ
english: Then, O king, the great chariot-warriors among the Saṃśaptakas loosed hundreds of thousands of smooth-jointed arrows upon Arjuna.

sanskrit: naiva kuntīsutaḥ pārtho naiva kṛṣṇo janārdanaḥ na hayā na ratho rājan dṛśyante sma śaraiś citāḥ
english: Then, O king, neither Pārtha the son of Kuntī, nor Kṛṣṇa Janārdana, nor the horses, nor the chariot could be seen, so thickly were they covered with arrows.
